reviews.review: pretty much the coolest game ever made

This is a review and a "guide" for those of you who are wondering what EDF5 is like.

Let's start with the cold, hard truth: Players jumping into the hardest missions on Inferno with less than 1,000 health and knowing they will die from almost anything hitting them isn't fun. And it's absolutely laughable when we see people with the starting 150/200/250 health join Inferno games. It's not fun for them, it's not fun for the players they're playing with, and people who do this are very likely to tell others the EDF franchise is terrible, never play it again, and never give any future EDF game a chance.

Is the beginning of EDF boring? Yes, terribly so. Your weapons suck, you've got long reload times, your cool mechas and tanks have horrendous controls and are the speed of slugs, your mobility options certainly don't feel like mobility options, enemies are slow, the first 40 missions are NPC dialogue slogs, enemies barely drop any loot so you don't feel like you're progressing, and you can't do anything cool, yet. If there's one thing I wish the development team would change, it's speeding up the abysmally slow beginning. At least make the mechs not so horrible in the beginning.

If you just started playing EDF: The best way to farm armor early game is to aim for 70% Completion. You will eventually be turning the armor/weapon limits off to grind to 100% Completion. There's going to be some kind of grind no matter what, the grind is central to EDF's gameplay loop.

Something you need to know: Playing the Single Player Mode scales the enemies to a single player. The game is much more manageable, but you'll have to gather loot by yourself. Playing Online Multiplayer causes the health of enemies to multiply, making it that much harder to flinch/kill enemies if you intend to play alone. Also, I don't think EDF is fun playing alone. You will have significantly more fun time playing with other people, especially if they're competent at the game.

Start by playing the game on Hard. EDF5 is generous that beating stages on Hard also gives you the medals for Easy and Normal. Do this with all 4 classes and you'll have 60% completion. Do note this is NOT true for EDF4.1, in that game, you have to do every single mission and mode. EDF4.1 is better in some ways compared to EDF5, but getting 70% Completion in 4.1 is as much of a pain in the ass as it sounds.

By 60% completion, including all of the mission failures you'll no doubt get, you should have a decent enough armor value on all classes to tackle Hardest and Inferno without dying instantly to stray crossfire from ant sprays, spider webs, artillery fire, sniper lasers, frog/cosmonaut bullets, tadpole dive bombing, etc. And most importantly, you won't die instantly to a gold ant spray unless you get shotgunned by them (IIRC a point-blank gold ant spray on Inferno does 32k-36k damage).

Most players will skip Hardest and go right into Inferno. I also recommend this, because the best weapons in the game drop in the latter half of Inferno. At this point, you only need 10% more completion to turn off the armor/weapon limit. That's about 200 missions of the 800 left you can spread among 4 classes. By this time, you should have at least 2k-3k health. That's enough to do Inferno, believe it or not. Your armor value isn't a measure of how "good" you are at EDF, like some players will tell you that you will no doubt encounter if you play online. It's just a number that lets you take more risks on higher difficulties without dying. At lower health, you just have to be very careful. This will also teach you that in order to complete the late game missions on Inferno, you have to have a plan, and the game is quick to show you when it doesn't work. If you're with a good team of players and you coordinate well, understand how to pick off single enemies in a group, know how to kite enemies, and understand what enemy threats need to get destroyed immediately, all while covering for your allies (without shooting them) while you're getting swarmed... you'll do alright.

It's going to suck jumping to Hardest/Inferno right away. You won't have decent weapons to do enough damage to enemies, so you and other people are just going to have to deal with you being kind of a liability first. In my experience, most people are pretty lenient on randoms with underpowered weapons. So long as you know how to play your class, don't hit your allies, don't aggro tons of enemies, don't charge in by yourself... or really, don't do anything stupid that causes constant wipes and therefore wasting peoples' time, people are pretty nice.

At this point, I recommend getting the DLC mission packs. Most of the latter half of Inferno missions let you use the DLC weapons, but you have to play the DLC missions on Inferno in order to get the DLC weapons. If you don't see the problem here: You'll going to be a liability again. Pray you get lucky and get the good DLC weapons first. I've been told DLC Pack 1 gives close-range DLC weapons while DLC Pack 2 gives long-range DLC weapons. I can't confirm this myself, I never paid attention to this.

Speaking of getting lucky, when you acquire weapons, they come with star rankings. Higher rankings mean the weapons are better, and your weapon stats will always be the highest gained from those random weapon drops. The biggest problem? It's random. You could get some good weapon stats very early. You may get them very late. It varies greatly and will affect your gameplay experience.

Weapon choices are not created equal. I know the developers are trying for a "use whatever weapons you want so long as you have fun", but it's hard to do that when a great majority of weapons suck even at max ranking. Not only that, some weapons are so ridiculously good, why would you use anything else? I'm looking at you, Phalanx and Thunder Crossbow.

EDF is a niche series. EDF games require time and energy before you feel like you're having "fun". The games have to hit you in just the right way to feel like it's something you want to be invested in. If it hits you in the right way, you'll get way more fun and entertainment out of EDF than a person reasonably should. If it doesn't, you won't make it past the beginning of the game. I've seen all too many Youtube and Twitch streamers thinking EDF is a "pick up and play" game that they'll have fun with right away. It isn't.

174.7 hours and counting, still only on mission 96. On singleplayer.

This game rules. Get it.
